classification.difficultyReason: Interpret radii, central heights and mutually perpendicular lengths before applying Pythagoras in several steps.

content.prompt: Calculate the value of $x$ in each of these diagrams, to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Horizontal cylinder with marked centre, radius dimension, dashed diameter and diagonal. Nonessential end-face shading is omitted.
spec.mathematics: Radius 3.7 m, diameter 7.4 m, diagonal 15.5 m and cylinder length x m.

spec.description: Square pyramid, equal adjacent base edges, central perpendicular height and labelled sloping edge. Decorative base fill is omitted.
spec.mathematics: Square side 3 cm, apex-to-corner length 5 cm, central height x cm.

answer.worked:
Let $r$ be the distance from the base centre to a corner.
$\begin{aligned}r^2&=1.5^2+1.5^2=4.5\\r&=\sqrt{4.5}\text{ cm}\\x^2&=5^2-(\sqrt{4.5})^2\\x&=\sqrt{20.5}\\x&\approx4.53\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

spec.description: Rectangular pyramid with central height, right-angle cue and unknown left sloping edge. Decorative base fill is omitted.
spec.mathematics: Base 3 m by 1.5 m; central perpendicular height 2 m; x is apex-to-corner distance.

answer.worked:
Let $r$ be the distance from the base centre to a corner.
$\begin{aligned}r^2&=1.5^2+0.75^2=2.8125\\r&=\sqrt{2.8125}\text{ m}\\x^2&=2^2+(\sqrt{2.8125})^2\\x&=\sqrt{6.8125}\\x&\approx2.61\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

spec.description: Triangular pyramid with three mutually perpendicular edges meeting at its hidden rear vertex; the cube-corner cue records all three right angles. Decorative base fill is omitted.
spec.mathematics: Apex-to-front lengths 5.31 cm and 4.04 cm; apex-to-rear length 2.93 cm; x is the front base edge.

answer.worked:
Let $a$ and $b$ be the two perpendicular base edges meeting at the rear vertex.
$\begin{aligned}a^2&=5.31^2-2.93^2=19.61\\a&=\sqrt{19.61}\text{ cm}\\b^2&=4.04^2-2.93^2=7.7367\\b&=\sqrt{7.7367}\text{ cm}\\x^2&=(\sqrt{19.61})^2+(\sqrt{7.7367})^2\\x&=\sqrt{27.3467}\\x&\approx5.23\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$
